sections.h2: What is Yellowstone County, Montana, and where is it?
sections.html:
Yellowstone County is the most populous county in Montana, with Billings as both its county seat and its largest city. It was created on February 26, 1883 and organized on May 1 of that year.

The county takes its name from the Yellowstone River, which roughly bisects it as it flows southwest to northeast. It covers 2,649 square miles, about 2,633 of them land, which makes it the 23rd largest Montana county by area. The 2020 census counted 164,731 residents, and the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate is 172,692, about 15% of the state's population.

For a seller, that scale means the county is not one market. A house in a Billings neighborhood, a farm parcel near Shepherd and a lot in a small town like Broadview are taxed by the same county offices but sit in very different school and utility districts.

sections.h2: Which towns and communities make up Yellowstone County?
sections.html:
Only two incorporated cities and one town sit inside the county: Billings, Laurel and Broadview. Most of the rest is unincorporated, and several communities are census-designated places.

TypePlaces
CitiesBillings (county seat), Laurel
TownBroadview
Census-designated placesActon, Ballantine, Custer, Huntley, Lockwood, Mountain View Colony, Nibbe, Pompeys Pillar, Shepherd, Worden
Other communitiesBillings Heights, Comanche, Hesper, Homewood Park, Newton, Yegen and others
Reservation landPart of the Crow Indian Reservation

That mix matters at closing. Property inside a city carries city levies on top of county and school levies, while a home in Lockwood or Huntley is billed by the county with its own school and special districts. Rural parcels may also involve well, septic and road access questions that a city lot never raises.

sections.h2: How do the roads, transit and schools work in Yellowstone County?
sections.html:
Interstate 90 and Interstate 94 both run through the county, along with U.S. 87, U.S. 212, U.S. 310 and Montana highways 3 and 47. Billings Metropolitan Transit, Express Arrow and Jefferson Lines provide public and intercity service.

School service is split across many districts. Three unified K-12 districts exist at Custer, Huntley Project and Lockwood. Billings, Broadview, Laurel and Shepherd have their own high school districts, and the county lists more than a dozen elementary districts, including Billings, Blue Creek, Canyon Creek, Elder Grove, Elysian, Independent, Laurel, Molt, Morin, Pioneer, Shepherd and Yellowstone Academy.

Your tax bill reflects whichever districts your parcel sits in, so two houses with the same value can have different bills. When you sell, buyers often compare those bills before anything else.

sections.h2: Who are the major employers in Yellowstone County?
sections.html:
Health care is a leading employer. Billings Clinic, which the Billings Chamber of Commerce calls Montana's largest independent health care system, reports more than 4,500 employees.

The county itself is a large collector of money. Its Treasurer's property tax department says it collects about $345 million in real and personal property taxes and processes roughly 75,000 real estate bills, 5,900 mobile home bills and 1,050 personal property bills every year. That volume explains why the office publishes precise due dates and strict penalties.

We could not confirm a current official list of the county's top employers, so we are not naming others here.

sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Yellowstone County?
sections.html:
The Yellowstone County Treasurer collects property tax, and the Montana Department of Revenue sets the values. The treasurer's page says Hank Peters serves as Treasurer, Assessor and Superintendent of Schools for the county.

  • Treasurer: Room 113, 2825 3rd Ave N, Billings, MT 59101
  • Mailing address: P.O. Box 35010, Billings, MT 59107
  • Phone: 406-256-2802
  • Tax Appeal Board: 406-256-2701, P.O. Box 35001, Billings

The office also records miscellaneous revenue, issues tax deeds and tax lien assignment certificates, and handles tax protests and mobile home moving permits. You can search records on the county's tax records search or read the property tax page.

sections.h2: When are Yellowstone County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Real estate tax is due in two halves, on November 30 and May 31, by 5 PM Mountain Time. If a date falls on a weekend or holiday, the next business day applies.

Tax typeFirst halfSecond half
Real estateNovember 30 (2026 only: December 3)May 31 (2027 only: June 1)
Mobile homeMay 31 (2027 only: June 1)November 30
Personal propertyJune 30None listed

Delinquent taxes carry a 2% penalty and interest of 5/6 of 1% each month. That applies to real property, personal property, mobile homes and farm and ranch property. Because the 2026 first-half date shifts to December 3, anyone closing in late November or early December should confirm which date the title company is using.

sections.h2: What happens to a Yellowstone County property with delinquent taxes?
sections.html:
The county attaches a tax lien and then allows a third party to buy an assignment of it. The treasurer's tax lien page says assignments are sold in late August, with a $50 fee for each assignment.

After that the sequence is slow and has several notice steps. Lienholders may pay later delinquent taxes on an assigned parcel only between June 1 and July 30 (June 2 to July 30 in 2027). In the final year of the redemption period, a notice that a tax deed may be issued goes out between May 1 and May 30. A tax deed carries a $25 deed fee plus recording fees of $20 for the first page and $10 for each added page.

The county says it does not give legal advice to people who buy tax liens. A seller with an assigned lien should treat it as a payoff item that the title company must clear, with the lienholder's interest and costs included.

The county's tax lien page keeps the list of certificates and the current rules, which changed after recent legislation.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Yellowstone County property valuation?
sections.html:
You object in writing within 30 days of the date on the classification and appraisal notice. That keeps your appeal alive for both years of the two-year valuation cycle on residential and commercial property.

The county's appeals page walks through the timing under Montana Code Annotated sections 15-7-102 and 15-15-102:

  • You may submit one application for reduction per valuation cycle.
  • An objection filed after 30 days applies only to the second year, and must be in by June 1 of that year.
  • The 30 days run from the date on the notice, not the date you received it, and no extra mailing days are added.
  • Only the County Tax Appeal Board can decide whether a late appeal had good cause, such as a notice mailed to the wrong address.

After an informal Department of Revenue review, you can appeal that result to the county board, and then to the State Tax Appeal Board. Boards may consider an actual selling price, independent appraisals and other evidence of market value. Completed forms go to the Clerk and Recorder's office.

sections.h2: How does a sale work when property tax is still owed in Yellowstone County?
sections.html:
The unpaid balance is settled out of the seller's proceeds at closing. The title company asks the Treasurer for the amount owed, including any penalty and monthly interest, and pays it from the sale.

A tax lien assigned to an investor adds the lienholder's costs, so ask for a written payoff before you accept a price. Pay by the due date if you can, because the 5/6 of 1% monthly interest keeps growing.

A cash buyer can close around a tax balance, since the payoff comes out of the sale. We buy houses as-is, and we do not promise a price before we see the property.

faqs.q: Who collects property tax in Yellowstone County?
faqs.a: The Yellowstone County Treasurer collects it, and the Montana Department of Revenue sets the values. The office is at 2825 3rd Ave N, Room 113 in Billings, and the phone number is 406-256-2802.

faqs.q: When is real estate tax due in Yellowstone County?
faqs.a: Real estate tax is due November 30 and May 31 by 5 PM Mountain Time, with the next business day applying on weekends and holidays. For 2026 the first half is due December 3, and for 2027 the second half is due June 1.

faqs.q: What is the late penalty in Yellowstone County?
faqs.a: Late taxes carry a 2% penalty plus interest of 5/6 of 1% per month. That applies to real property, personal property, mobile homes and farm and ranch property.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal my valuation in Yellowstone County?
faqs.a: You have 30 days from the date on the appraisal notice for the appeal to cover the full two-year cycle. A later appeal applies only to the second year and must be filed by June 1.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Yellowstone County house if there is a tax lien?
faqs.a: Yes. The lien and any related costs are paid from your proceeds at closing, so you need a written payoff from the Treasurer and any lienholder before closing.

faqs.q: Where do I file a tax appeal in Yellowstone County?
faqs.a: You can file an informal review with the Department of Revenue or appeal to the County Tax Appeal Board. Mail the form to the Clerk and Recorder at P.O. Box 35001, Billings, MT 59101.
